sights.address: Near JR Ōtori Station, Sakai, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: Ichinomiya (first shrine) of old Izumi Province, c. 1,900 years old, enshrining Yamato Takeru; a five-minute walk from JR Ōtori Station.
Ancient Kōyasan Shingon temple (founded 701, restored by Kūkai 815) holding the National Treasure Nyoirin Kannon and Kondō hall; plum, cherry and autumn-leaf spot.
Mountain temple patronised by Toyotomi Hideyoshi (his letter survives here), with National Treasure Buddhist statues shown in autumn special exhibitions.

sights.n: Chikatsu Asuka Museum (大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館)
sights.w: Tadao Ando's stepped kofun-shaped museum of Japan's burial-mound age, set in the Chikatsu Asuka Fudoki-no-Oka tomb park.
Sakai Zen temple founded by Miyoshi Nagayoshi, burned in the 1615 Siege of Osaka and rebuilt by the monk Takuan in 1617; tea-ceremony links to Sen no Rikyū.
Temple founded 744 whose 1834 three-storey pagoda is the only one standing in Osaka Prefecture; reached on the retro Showa-era Mizuma Railway.

sights.address: In front of Hamadera Ekimae / Hamadera-kōen Station, Sakai & Takaishi, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: One of the prefecture's oldest parks (1873), a seaside pine grove at the end of the Hankai tram; the Tatsuno Kingo-office Hamadera-kōen station building is a rare Meiji survivor.
Museum of the Kishiwada Danjiri Matsuri — the September festival where carved wooden floats are hauled at a run round street corners.
Hundertwasser-designed waste plant on an artificial island — red, black and white walls, a golden onion tower and roof greenery; free guided interior tours by reservation.

sights.address: Tempozan Park, Chikkō, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: 'Japan's lowest mountain' — a 4.5 m summit marker inside a harbourside park with a hidden cherry-blossom grove and an Emperor Meiji monument; 7 min from Osakakō Station.

sights.address: Tempozan Harbor Village, 1 Kaigan-dōri, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: The harbour mall at the heart of Tempozan Harbor Village, beside the Ferris wheel and Kaiyūkan; inside are the retro Shōwa food alley Naniwa Kuishinbo Yokochō and LEGOLAND Discovery Center Osaka.
Kawachi's ichinomiya at the foot of the Ikoma range, said to date back 2,600+ years; famous for its plum grove and the 23 December 'laughing ritual' (Owarai Shinji).

sights.n: Ishikiri Tsurugiya Shrine (石切劔箭神社)
sights.w: 'Ishikiri-san', the god of swellings — nationally known for the ohyakudo-mairi, worshippers circling between the stones and the hall, and a fortune-teller-lined approach street.
Japan's largest greenhouse botanical garden, built as Osaka's pavilion for Expo '90 in Tsurumi Ryokuchi Park — ~15,000 plants of 5,500 species.
Birthplace of Japanese malt whisky (built 1923): whisky museum, paid tastings and a lottery-entry production tour; 10 min walk from JR Yamazaki / Hankyu Ōyamazaki.

sights.n: Open-Air Museum of Old Japanese Farmhouses (日本民家集落博物館)
sights.w: Japan's first open-air museum (1956), in Hattori Ryokuchi Park: 11 relocated 17th-19th-century folk houses from Iwate to Amami Ōshima.
En no Gyōja-founded temple on the Minoo Falls trail, home to one of Japan's four great Benzaiten and billed as the birthplace of the Japanese lottery; 15 min walk from Hankyu Minoh.
Shrine to Ame-no-Iwafune, a 12 m boat-shaped boulder up the Amanogawa valley; the 'iwa-kuguri' rock-cave crawl beneath the giant stones is open to visitors.

sights.n: Hirakatashuku Kagiya Museum (枚方宿鍵屋資料館)
sights.w: Edo-period riverside inn where travellers waited for the Fushimi-Osaka riverboats on the Kyō-kaidō post town; a cultural property, opened as a museum in 2001.

sights.n: Engyō-ji (Mount Shosha, 書写山圓教寺)
sights.w: Atmospheric 1,000-year-old mountain temple complex 30 min from Himeji by bus and ropeway; the Mitsunodō halls were a set for The Last Samurai.
Kōyasan's central temple complex, founded where Kūkai found his thrown sankosho in a pine; dominated by the Kondō hall and the vermilion Konpon Daitō pagoda.

sights.n: Furuichi Kofun Group — Konda Gobyōyama Kofun (誉田御廟山古墳)
sights.w: The second-largest keyhole tomb in Japan (attributed to Emperor Ōjin), heart of the Furuichi half of the UNESCO Mozu-Furuichi kofun group, next to Konda Hachimangū near Kintetsu Furuichi Station.

sights.address: Kongō range, Chihaya-Akasaka village, Osaka / Nara border, Japan
sights.w: Osaka's highest peak (1,125 m) and the prefecture's favourite hike — ropeway, summit shrine and frosted-tree winter scenery in the Kongō-Ikoma-Kisen Quasi-National Park.

sights.address: Senri Banpaku Kōen, Suita, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: Entertainment complex beside Expo '70 Park: the Kaiyūkan team's 'living museum' NIFREL and Japan's tallest Ferris wheel, plus a large mall.

sights.n: Hoshida Park — Hoshi no Buranko suspension bridge (星のブランコ)
sights.address: Osaka Prefectural Forest Hoshida Park, Katano, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: Japan's largest wooden pedestrian suspension bridge, the 'Star Swing', strung across a valley of the Tanabata-legend Amanogawa forest above Katano.

sights.n: Hanazono Rugby Stadium (東大阪市花園ラグビー場)
sights.w: Japan's oldest rugby-only stadium (1929), the 'holy ground' of the national high-school tournament and a 2019 Rugby World Cup venue; free Hanazono Rugby Museum on match days.

sights.n: Fujita Museum of Art (藤田美術館)
sights.w: Meiji magnate Fujita Denzaburō's collection of ~2,000 Asian artworks — 9 National Treasures (incl. a yōhen tenmoku tea bowl) and 53 Important Cultural Properties — in a rebuilt gallery by Kyōbashi.

sights.n: Shiba Ryōtarō Memorial Museum (司馬遼太郎記念館)
sights.w: The historical novelist's house and study beside a Tadao Ando library hall whose 11 m wall of shelves holds part of his 60,000-book collection.

sights.n: Panasonic Museum (Kōnosuke Matsushita History Museum, Kadoma)
sights.w: Free museum at Panasonic's Kadoma home: founder Matsushita Kōnosuke's story, the 'Monozukuri-ism' hall of landmark home appliances, and Sakura Square.

sights.n: Kyocera Dome Osaka (京セラドーム大阪)
sights.w: Kansai's largest indoor stadium (36,220 seats for baseball), home of the Orix Buffaloes and Osaka's big-concert dome; Tugboat Taishō waterfront food-and-art strip is a short walk away.

sights.address: Chikkō Red Brick Warehouse, Chikkō, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: Classic-car museum of about 80 landmark cars (e.g. a 1900-1950 Rolls-Royce Phantom II era line-up) inside the 1923 Chikkō red-brick port warehouse near Tempozan.

sights.n: Osaka Maishima Seaside Park (大阪まいしまシーサイドパーク)
sights.w: Seasonal flower park on Maishima island (formerly the Maishima Lily Garden): about a million nemophila against the bay in April, lilies in early summer.

sights.n: Ikeda Castle Ruins Park (池田城跡公園)
sights.w: Park (2000) on the site of the Ikeda clan's castle: stroll garden with a central pond, tea room and a lookout tower with views to Takarazuka, Osaka and Kobe.

sights.n: Satsukiyama Park & Zoo (五月山公園・五月山動物園)
sights.w: Ikeda's hillside park for spring cherry blossom and autumn leaves; at its foot the free Satsukiyama Zoo, Japan's second-smallest, famous for its wombats.

sights.n: Itsuō Art Museum & Kobayashi Ichizō Memorial Hall (逸翁美術館)
sights.w: Collection of Hankyu/Takarazuka founder Kobayashi Ichizō (pen-name Itsuō) — early-modern paintings and tea ceramics — beside his Gazoku Sansō residence, now the memorial hall.

sights.n: Kobe Earthquake Memorial Museum (人と防災未来センター)
sights.address: HAT Kobe, Chūō-ku, Kobe, Hyōgo, Japan
sights.w: Memorial museum of the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake (opened 2002): a large-screen recreation of the quake, a recovery documentary and hands-on disaster-prevention exhibits.
Early-20th-century landscape garden of former Kobe mayor Kodera Kenkichi, public since 1941, with a relocated Western-style residence and boathouse; 300 yen, closed Thursdays.

sights.n: Kobe City Museum (神戸市立博物館)
sights.address: Old Settlement (Kyūkyoryūchi), Chūō-ku, Kobe, Hyōgo, Japan
sights.w: Archaeology and one of the world's largest collections of Namban art — Japanese painting from the first contact with Western ships in the 1500s — in a former bank in the old foreign settlement.

sights.n: Osaka Museum of Housing and Living (大阪くらしの今昔館)
sights.w: Walk-through, life-size reconstruction of an Edo-period Osaka merchant townscape on the upper floors of a building at the north end of Tenjinbashi-suji.
